asf-mdp384-c76r.summary: The writer reports that the French ambassador at Rome advised his young King (taken to be Henri II) to keep what his father left him rather than seek glory in a war; but the King's ardour, encouraged by great men of France, cannot be held back, and the ambassador is urged to work for union with England.
asf-mdp384-c76r.en:
Copy of a chapter of a letter from Rome of 10 August 1547.

The ambassador of France, by way of a short discourse, wrote some days ago to his King that the greatest glory he could win
at this beginning of his reign was simply to look to his own guard, to keep what his father had left him and to govern
himself well; and that the desire to gain by breaking into war went against him, since he saw in it many great dangers;
and that he should consider that he was young and had time to take up better occasions than these, which God would show
him at one time or another; and so he counselled and dissuaded him otherwise.

system: Homophonic substitution with a prefix code: 6, 8, 9 alone = e, o, a, other codes two digits (10 = che, 24 = et), dotted variants equal, nomenclature codes for names.
